notes: Educational simulation. Real airline, airport and aircraft identities; every performance and financial figure is synthetic. No airline ranking represents actual performance.

Period: 1 January–31 December 2025. Exactly 1,000 scheduled sectors per airline. These selected-route samples are not complete airline networks. Source pages checked 1 November 2026 establish fleet/route compatibility, not a reconstruction of every 2025 departure.

Each airline has two synthetic aircraft IDs, not real registrations. Aircraft-day denominators include all 365 days, including idle days. Utilisation measures only sampled flying, not actual airline or whole-fleet utilisation. Recovery/repositioning is outside scope; this is not a dispatch or crew-legality model.

Summer schedule counts and passenger demand rise with airline-specific variation. December includes a holiday uplift. Demand, capacity, fares and costs vary separately. Model differences are teaching assumptions, not measured airline characteristics.

All distances are rounded great-circle estimates from approximate airport coordinates; not actual flown tracks. Both flight directions are included. Codes and airport names identify real airports; coordinates are teaching approximations.

Cancelled sectors have zero passengers, traffic, block hours and offered operated capacity, but positive cancellation costs. Delay and turnaround are blank when inapplicable. Diversions count as operated and not on time; planned sector distance is retained as a teaching convention.

OTP: arrival delay under 15 minutes and not diverted, divided by all operated sectors. Early arrivals are on time. Mean delay uses max(delay,0) over operated sectors. Turnaround observations apply only to the second leg in each simulated pair; minimum turn times are planning assumptions, not observed minima.
All passengers are treated as revenue passengers. Physical seat configurations are representative. Available seats assume all installed seats offered; blocked business seats are not modelled.

Cargo is belly freight only, excluding passenger baggage. Cargo capacity is a conservative synthetic commercial allocation, not certified payload. No cargo service is modelled for Ryanair: CTK=0, ACTK=0 and CLF is not applicable.

Baggage kg refers to checked baggage. Delayed, lost and damaged bags are mutually exclusive final categories. A bag later declared lost is not counted again as delayed. Complaint and compliment counts are submissions, not unique people.

All finance uses EUR, with no exchange-rate inference. Passenger revenue excludes ancillary/cargo revenue. RASK includes all three. CASK includes allocated operating costs including depreciation and cancellation costs. Monthly finances reconcile to the selected flights; debt and cash balances describe the simulation only.

Debt and closing cash are stocks: select the latest month, never sum across months. Profit and cash flows are period totals. Financial balance and utilisation KPIs are unavailable under route/distance filters because their denominators and allocations have a different scope.
Excel source tables are editable; summary formulas recalculate in Excel. HTML embeds a fixed copy of the same baseline dataset. Editing Excel does not automatically update HTML.
AI disclosure: dataset, explanations and software prepared with assistance from OpenAI ChatGPT. Lecturer: Dr. Bahtiyar Eren. Review assumptions before teaching or further analysis.
